title: Home
text:
Welcome to my portfolio for MUSA 5080: Public Policy Analytics at the University of Pennsylvania.
This site documents my work in the Master of Urban Spatial Analytics program — weekly notes, course assignments, and a final project applying data analysis to urban policy questions.



Hi! I’m a student in the MUSA program at Penn. My background is in GIS, and I’m interested in GIS.




Weekly Notes — what I’m learning each week
Assignments — analyses completed for the course
About — more background and how to reach me






Email: alimuro1@upenn.edu
GitHub: @chloealimurong

title: Week 1: Getting Set Up
text:
What is a website?
a folder of html files → quarto
&
a computer always on → github pages (free)
What is quarto?
RENDER
.qmd (i write) → quarto (machine) → .html (webpage)
What happens in the machine?

Read file top to bottom
Finds code chunks
Sends chunks to R and gets results back
Glues text into HTML

Anatomy of qmd
YAML
markdown (own writing)
code chunks
Files + F
What is “index”
Website rule: Ask for a folder, get folders (index.html)
name.github.io/ → docs/index.html
/weekly-notes/ → docs/weekly-notes/index.html
GIT/ version tracker, invisible, runs on own computer
Github.com/ website that stores copy of folder
GitHub Desktop/ buttons that tell Git what to do

Commit: “save a labeled snapshot” (lives on computer)
Push: “send snapshot to Github.com”
R script: code only, sandbox

title: About
text: Before MUSA, I did a couple different things. I was a part of NASA DEVELOP where I conducted a spatial and temporal analysis of landfill methane emissions in New Hampshire. I also worked for the DC Govt. where I helped manage their database systems (enterprise and through GitHub and ArcGIS). I did a recent project for Mapping Black California where I rebuilt their Stop the Hate Dashboard that helps users identify hate crime patterns across California based on demographic and time. Right now, I help Spectrum (Charter Communications) map rural America and their internet serviceability. I became interested in Urban Spatial Analytics when I took an applied Social Statistics class where I could gather public data and make meaningful analyses with it. I hope to continue that throughout and after MUSA.
